chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about gloom (melancholy/sorrow), so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to eat grapes.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What did Allah command a Prophet to eat to cure his gloom?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the therapeutic efficacy of grapes (*‘Inab*) for alleviating melancholy (*Ghamm*), reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing natural remedies as divinely ordained signs. It underscores the holistic approach in Prophetic medicine, where specific foods are prescribed not merely for nutrition but for spiritual and emotional healing, a concept deeply rooted in the broader Islamic understanding of *Tibb al-Nabawi*.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the Prophets<sup>as</sup> complained to Allah<sup>as</sup> Mighty and Majestic of the gloom, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commanded him<sup>as</sup> with eating the grapes’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih in a marfu ‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One of the Prophets complained before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, about sadness and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, commanded him to eat grapes.’”
